answer: Edge-disjoint neighbor entry gate. A new agent gets full routing weight only when its declared peers form at least three edge-disjoint paths into separate active clusters, and its neighbor overlap with any single cluster stays under a fixed cap. An attacker must maintain three independent live links per identity, each anchored in a different cluster, so mass duplication multiplies upkeep. The reef cluster's cap blocks copy-paste peer lists. Basalt anchors one required path. A zephyr of peer churn resets the gate.
